name: Eliam
overview: Eliam is a male figure known primarily as the father of Bathsheba, a significant character in the biblical narrative. While his tribal affiliation and additional details are not recorded, his mention establishes a familial link important to the unfolding events in 2 Samuel. There are no further notes expanding on his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliam means 'G-d is my kinsman,' reflecting a personal acknowledgment of God's protective relationship. Another form of the name, Ammiel, shares the same meaning, emphasizing the theme of divine kinship. These names highlight a theological truth embedded in his identity, though they were not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Eliam as the father of Bathsheba, linking him to a key biblical family line. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Eliam's significance arises chiefly through his daughter Bathsheba, whose story intersects with King David's reign and God's providential plan. Though Eliam himself is not the focus of narrative action, his mention grounds Bathsheba's lineage and situates the unfolding drama within a real family context. This connection underscores the biblical theme of God's sovereign involvement in human history through ordinary individuals.
